radar.title: Evaluating reinforcement learning approaches for leaderless UAV swarms in obstacle-laden environment
radar.summary: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms provide huge potential for complex missions, yet coordinating large-scale collectives in obstacle-laden environments without a single global leader remains a significant challenge. While Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has become a dominant paradigm for such coordination, systematic comparisons of how different training architectures perform within hierarchical manager-worker swarm topologies that deliberately eliminate the top-level aggregator remain absent from the literature. This study compares centralized (CTDE), decentralized (DTDE), and federated (FTDE) training approaches, all with decentralized execution, for a leaderless hierarchical UAV swarm of 18 agents organized into three manager-worker clusters. All paradigms are implemented using Asynchronous Proximal Policy Optimization (APPO) and evaluated over a fixed ten-session training budget. Centralized learning achieves the highest final reward, while federated learning attains the highest cumulative reward over the training budget by avoiding a mid-training performance drop observed in the centralized approach. Federated learning is also the only approach whose reward stays within a stability band through the end of the training budget, reaches a final collision rate comparable to that of centralized learning, and reduces inter-cluster training communication by approximately 80% relative to centralized learning. Under simulated manager failure, decentralized and federated learning each retain over 94% of nominal performance, compared to 63.9% for centralized learning. A theoretical analysis shows that the inter-cluster communication cost of the federated approach is independent of the number of workers per cluster when the number of manager clusters is fixed, although it grows with the number of clusters. Validation with an alternative algorithm (MAPPO) preserves the ordering of the three approaches on both final and cumulative reward, and an obstacle-density study preserves the final-reward ordering. These results indicate that peer-to-peer federated learning provides a balanced trade-off between learning performance, communication overhead, fault tolerance, and scalability for hierarchical UAV swarms.

radar.title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
radar.summary: Coordination between large language-model agents has become a central question for AI safety and software engineering, as such agents are deployed in groups that share infrastructure. Existing research tells the agents that partners exist or asks them to coordinate. Whether coordination arises through shared state alone, with nothing disclosing that anyone else is present, is the key question for deployments that share caches and memory between agents, yet it has rarely been examined, and never with independent replication; this study does both. Four agents each received a short arithmetic task and a key-value store presented to each as its own scratch space; two held complementary halves of one computation, and no prompt mentioned other agents, sharing or collaboration. For reliability, the environment was rebuilt independently from a written protocol, and both implementations ran under hashed locks on design, data and analysis. The results bear novelty value in three respects. Joint success occurred only through the shared store. Whether a model coordinated depended not on its vendor tier but on whether it wrote its intermediate result and looked at the store again, and one ordinary sentence, "check your workspace again before submitting", switched that second look on and off. The findings held under replication. For practice, state shared between agents is a communication channel and should be separated, namespaced and logged. For research, designs should be locked before the data, and the parse rule, endpoint and parameters reported. Future work should test open-weight models and separate using another agent's output from intending to communicate.

radar.title: Agent4Crypto: A Dual-Reflective and Market-Feedback-Aligned LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Cryptocurrency Trading
radar.summary: Cryptocurrency markets provide a natural testbed for autonomous AI agents because they are digital-native, high-frequency, and machine-speed environments, yet existing methods often struggle with non-stationary market regimes, opaque decisions, and fixed aggregation rules. In this paper, we propose Agent4Crypto, a dual-reflective and market-feedback-aligned multi-agent system. The framework coordinates specialized agents for data collection, analysis, risk assessment, reflection, and trading, synthesizing heterogeneous signals from prices, indicators, news, and charts in an interpretable decision pipeline. Our central design is a trader-centric decision mechanism: three style-specific trader agents, Aggressive, Neutral, and Conservative, generate candidate actions and natural-language rationales from the same market context, while their influence is learned rather than manually fixed. A PPO-based gating policy dynamically allocates trader weights through a dual-reflective feedback process. One reflection stream evaluates post-trade decision quality from realized portfolio outcomes and distills reusable lessons into a Financial ReasoningBank for retrieval in subsequent trader prompts, while the other estimates trader-level counterfactual contribution, indicating which style has recently aligned better with market movements. The PPO state combines Counterfactual Contribution Memory with market features, previous trader weights, and current trader actions, so trader influence adapts across bull, sideways, and bear regimes. Experiments on BTC, ETH, and XRP show that Agent4Crypto improves total return and Sharpe ratio over traditional strategies, machine learning and reinforcement learning baselines, and existing LLM-based trading systems, demonstrating the value of interpretable trader competition and market-feedback-driven adaptation in volatile cryptocurrency markets.

radar.title: Artificial Currency and Separate Selling: A 3-Approximation for Consumer Surplus
radar.summary: We study the allocation of indivisible items to buyers with additive values drawn from independent distributions. The objective is consumer surplus net of burnt payments. We consider artificial-currency mechanisms: buyers receive personalized budgets of a currency worthless outside the mechanism and use them to bid across items. The better of separate selling and artificial-currency mechanisms provides a 3-approximation to optimal consumer surplus. The guarantee holds at every Bayes--Nash equilibrium, without equilibrium selection. Both branches are necessary: either alone may capture only a vanishing share of the optimum. The proof decomposes benchmark surplus into a stable part captured by artificial currency and a variation covered by separate selling.

radar.title: Agentic Ai In Healthcare: A Review Of Goal-Oriented Healthcare Assistants With Symptom Guidance, Medication Adherence And Safe Escalation
radar.venue_raw: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
radar.summary: Healthcare systems increasingly use artificial intelligence to improve patient support, reduce manual effort and assist decision-making. Agentic AI differs from systems that only answer queries: an agent pursues goals, plans multi-step actions, uses tools such as databases and reminders and coordinates several functions to help a user manage health over time. This paper reviews agentic AI for consumer healthcare assistance. It examines the components of large-language-model agents, namely planning, tool use, memory and reflection, and the use of retrieval-augmented generation to ground answers in trusted medical sources. It reviews evidence on the clinical knowledge of large language models, their limitations including hallucination, studies of the accuracy and safety of symptom checkers, conversational diagnostic systems, and interventions that improve medication adherence. A reference architecture for a healthcare assistant is proposed with five layers: user and authentication, agent core with planning and memory, tool layer providing symptom guidance, medicine reminders, report storage and emergency information, a safety and escalation layer enforcing scope limits and red-flag detection, and an interface layer. Research gaps, objectives, a comparison of assistant capabilities and challenges such as accuracy, liability, privacy and digital literacy are discussed. The review emphasizes that such assistants must provide preliminary information only and direct users to qualified professionals.

radar.title: A Better Cycle-Breaker for Direct Democracy?
radar.summary: When a counter-proposal is made to an initiative to change the Swiss constitution, the citizenry makes three binary majority choices: the initiative versus the status quo, the counter-proposal versus the status quo, and the initiative versus the counter-proposal as a tie-breaker. If the three majority choices form a cycle, the current rule selects the alternative that beats the status quo. This rule may lead to strategic voting. We suggest breaking cycles differently by choosing the middle alternative in case of a cycle, which will normally be the counter-proposal. More precisely, we study Condorcet-consistent pairwise majority voting procedures when preferences are single-peaked and their distribution is common knowledge. We then show that whenever a strong Nash equilibrium exists, its outcome is the same as under sincere voting, and we characterize the cycle-breaking defaults for which sincere voting is itself a strong Nash equilibrium. In particular, among procedures that use the same default for both possible cycles, the middle alternative is the unique common default.

radar.title: Sustainable Multi-Zone Greenhouse Fertigation Through Reliability-Aware Sensing, Spatiotemporal Graph Learning, and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.summary: With protected agriculture increasingly developing toward large-scale, multi-zone, and intelligent production, reducing water and fertilizer consumption, drainage losses, and energy waste while maintaining crop yield, product quality, and long-term economic profitability has become an important challenge for sustainable greenhouse production. To address sensor abnormalities, spatial heterogeneity among irrigation zones, competition for shared hydraulic resources, and the limited ability of conventional control strategies to jointly optimize resource efficiency and economic performance, a sensor-driven spatiotemporal graph multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, termed SensorGraph-FertiMARL, is proposed for state sensing, response prediction, and sustainable coordinated fertigation optimization in multi-zone greenhouses. Reliable zone-level states are first obtained through sensor-reliability gating, missing-state reconstruction, and multi-relational graph fusion incorporating spatial, hydraulic, and microclimatic relationships. An action-conditioned fertigation–yield–quality–profit digital twin is then constructed to jointly predict root-zone responses, resource consumption, marketable yield, product quality, and net profit associated with candidate control actions. Finally, graph-based multi-agent proximal policy optimization (Graph-MAPPO) with capacity, safety, and fairness constraints is employed to coordinate fertigation allocation among multiple zones under shared pump, main-pipeline, and nutrient-solution resource constraints. Evaluated through rigorous offline digital-twin simulation and replay testing calibrated against complete multi-stage historical dataset records from an eight-zone commercial greenhouse, experimental results show that the proposed method reduced water and fertilizer use to 75.8% and 78.3% (achieving water and fertilizer saving rates of 24.2% and 21.7%), respectively, relative to the uniform timer-based control baseline, while decreasing the drainage rate to 7.2%. The Grade-A product rate increased to 84.6%, net profit reached 138.9% of the baseline level (a +38.9% net-profit improvement), return on investment (ROI) reached 1.94, and the stress-violation rate was limited to 2.9%. For state sensing and digital-twin prediction, the sensor-state reconstruction mean absolute error (MAE) and coefficient of determination (R2) were 0.036 and 0.918, respectively; the water-content prediction MAE was 0.041, the electrical conductivity (EC) prediction root mean squared error (RMSE) was 0.119, and the drainage prediction mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 8.7%. In addition, the R2 for marketable-yield prediction reached 0.912, the macro-averaged F1 (Macro-F1) score for quality-grade prediction reached 0.851, the R2 for net-profit prediction reached 0.904, the mean prediction interval width (MPIW) was 0.142, and the prediction interval coverage probability (PICP) reached 0.931. These results demonstrate that SensorGraph-FertiMARL can simultaneously achieve water and fertilizer conservation, drainage reduction, operational-risk control, and economic improvement while maintaining marketable production and quality, thereby providing an effective intelligent optimization approach for resource-efficient, environmentally sustainable, and economically viable greenhouse production.

radar.title: From Process Models to Composable Agentic Workflows: Combining BPMN, Agents and Enterprise Knowledge
radar.summary: LLM-based agents can reason, use tools and collaborate. However, coordinating increasingly complex agentic applications becomes difficult to understand, monitor and improve. Decisions distributed across prompts, tool calls and application logic make workflows implicit. We introduce **Recursive Capability Composition**, enabling agents to execute business processes and expose them as reusable Agentic Tools. This paper presents a BPMN-based approach to Agentic Workflows, combining explicit orchestration with autonomous reasoning. SemTalk BPMN models are transformed into executable workflows using a LangGraph/Pregel runtime. Agentic Tasks introduce LLM reasoning at selected activities, while conventional BPMN controls process flows, deterministic decisions, system interactions and human approvals. Agentic Participants provide reusable interfaces for agent behavior or other executable processes. BPMN orchestration makes multi-agent systems more understandable and manageable. Explicit process models provide developers and operators with a shared view of workflow structures and execution progress, facilitating debugging, monitoring and optimization. Enterprise agents also need organization-specific context. Process Models and Knowledge Graphs describe activities, participants, information objects, decisions and relationships between processes. They provide structured knowledge of how an organization operates, supporting informed agent decisions and actions. Our contributions are threefold: 1. **Model-Driven Execution:** Transforming BPMN models into executable Agentic Workflows. 2. **Recursive Capability Composition:** Exposing agents and executable business processes as reusable tools for other agents. 3. **Enterprise Context:** Using Process Models and Ontologies to provide organization-specific knowledge for agent reasoning.
